no_mask.p2_rule_retired: D(t) <= S(t) on >= 90% of steps, both channels, both shapes; a P2 fail cancels the outcome run, a P2 pass admits nothing; the outcome run decides. Retired 2026-10-01 by Fable: unsatisfiable under an exchangeable null: per-step P(D<=S) = 1/5; fails a correct candidate at step 1 where S = 0 (perf lane's AUDIT/tierb-nomask-2026-10-01/p2_null_sim.out: 0 of 200 null candidates pass).
no_mask.p2_rule: P2 (amended 2026-10-01 by Fable; supersedes the D(t)<=S(t)-on->=90%-of-steps rule, which no exchangeable null can satisfy: per step P(D<=S) = C(3,2)/C(6,2) = 1/5, distribution-free; aggregation and calibration amended again 2026-10-01 by Fable after c18d245's calibration, see p2_amendment_2). Arms: the 3 masked baselines B_j and the 3 no-mask candidates M_i of one shape, default kernels, same batches. Refuse (no verdict) unless: >= 3 baselines and >= 1 candidate; one consumed_digest; equal steps and channel lengths; every arm termination == 'steps_exhausted'; every baseline row train_attention_mask == 'padding' and every candidate row == 'none'. Per channel in (letter, span): live = steps where any arm is non-zero; a channel with no live step is not_run. Per step set T in {first live step, all live steps}: bbar(t) = mean_j B_j(t); L = mean over T of bbar(t), L > 0 else not_run; dev_i = mean over T of (M_i(t) - bbar(t)) / L per candidate; noise_j = mean over T of (B_j(t) - mean_{k!=j} B_k(t)) / L per baseline; dev = max_i |dev_i|; noise = max_j |noise_j|; tau = 0.02; kappa = 3. Verdict(channel, T) = inconclusive if noise > tau/kappa; else fail if dev > tau; else pass. Channel = worst over T, report-only. Shape, from its four applications (channel, T): fail iff every application is pass or fail and at least one is fail; else not_run iff any application is not_run; else inconclusive iff any application is inconclusive; else pass. The row always records fail_applications, the list of (channel, T) whose verdict is fail, in channel order (letter, span) then T order (first, all), empty when none; on a held shape it is what the human reads first. Gate: item 9 goes iff both shapes' latest verdict is pass. fail cancels it. not_run or missing cancels it until a rerun. inconclusive holds it for the human: not a fail, the gate stays closed, no override flag, env var or --tau; the human either amends tau here (recorded) and the lane changes the module constant by commit and recomputes --p2 from the saved result rows (no GPU), so the new verdict row supersedes, or drops the candidate. A pass admits nothing; the outcome run decides. The verdict row records tau, kappa and, per (channel, T): L, every dev_i, every noise_j, dev, noise; each arm's train_path; and the per-step profile (median and max of D and S, fraction D<=S, first step with D > max S, final losses), all report-only. Calibration, by CPU simulation against the implemented function, committed under AUDIT/tierb-nomask-2026-10-01/ before any GPU P2 session. The configuration universe (n=100 and n=50, 3v3 and 3v1, with and without bit-identical baseline forwards) applies to every target unless the target names its own: exchangeable null at the p2_null_sim noise model: pass >= 99%, fail 0; the same null at noise x3, x5, x10, x20, x100: fail <= 12% at every multiplier and configuration, the split reported together with the count of held shapes (inconclusive or not_run) that carried a failing application; all candidates x(1+delta): delta 0.5% pass >= 99%, delta 1% pass >= 99%, delta 3% fail >= 99%, delta 4% fail >= 99%; delta 2% (= tau: the boundary by construction, each application a coin flip whatever the noise, 3v1 passing about 1/16) is run and its split reported, with no target; one candidate x1.04 with two null (3v3 by construction): fail >= 99%; step-1-only x1.03 with bit-identical baseline forwards: fail >= 99%, and x1.01: pass >= 99%; Gaussian single-application worst case of P(fail | null) over sigma/tau: <= 4.5%.

p2_amendment_2.recorded: 2026-10-01, Fable, after the calibration committed at c18d245 (75 of 78 met) and before any GPU P2 session
p2_amendment_2.misses: x20 n=100 3v3 noisy step 0: fail 12.1% vs <= 12%; delta 2% 3v1 noisy step 0: fail 92.6% (n=100) and 91.0% (n=50) vs >= 95%
p2_amendment_2.scope: the configuration list is the harness's universe for every target unless a target names its own; the strict reading the lane ran is right and is now in the rule; 3v1 stays because the rule accepts >= 1 candidate
p2_amendment_2.delta_2: a target at delta = tau is unsatisfiable for one candidate under any tau and kappa: dev sits at tau plus a symmetric error, each application fails ~50%, the shape passes ~1/16; 3v3 met it only by the max over three candidates and any-fail over four applications, the bit-identical rows only by float rounding (0.020000000000000018 > 0.02). A mis-specified target, not a rule failure: retired to report-only; delta 3% (1.5 tau, the step-1 x1.03 placement) fail >= 99% and delta 1% (0.5 tau) pass >= 99% added at every configuration
p2_amendment_2.x20: every one of the 121 fails had an inconclusive sibling application (p2_miss_diag.out). The mechanism is the any-fail union over four applications and three candidates of a per-application worst case the Gaussian target permits (<= 4.5% each, ~17% as a union), so the <= 12% shape target and the <= 4.5% application target were never jointly satisfiable as written. The defect is the aggregation: a shape was cancelled with no human look on one application's fail while three said the noise was unresolvable. Fixed there: fail is terminal only when every application is conclusive; otherwise the shape is held and names its failing applications. The <= 12% bound is kept, not moved, because any number chosen now is chosen after seeing 12.1%; x5 is added to the grid because an all-conclusive requirement is most exposed between x3 and x10
p2_amendment_2.statistic_unchanged: dev_i, noise_j, tau = 0.02, kappa = 3 and the per-application verdict are untouched; noise_j stays a draw from dev_i's own null distribution rather than a pooled per-step sd scaled by 1/sqrt(n), because real nondeterministic runs diverge and stay diverged and the pooled estimator would understate the mean's error
p2_amendment_2.gate_unchanged: p2_gate, the --p2 exit codes (0 pass, 1 fail, 2 else) and the gate CLI are untouched; pass still requires every application to pass
p2_amendment_2.hold_reading: On an inconclusive or not_run shape the human reads, per application: verdict, every dev_i, every noise_j, then fail_applications and the step-1 dev. A first-step application with noise 0 (bit-identical baseline forwards) and dev > tau is a kernel-level difference on identical weights: drop the candidate. An application with every dev_i <= tau and noise > tau/kappa is the screen's resolution, not the candidate's shift: the human may amend tau here (recorded) per the existing clause, rerun both sessions, or drop. Nothing here is automated; the gate stays closed until a pass row exists
p2_amendment_2.q3_gate_kept: the screen stays a gate: pass -> item 9 goes; fail (all four conclusive) -> cancelled; inconclusive/not_run -> held for the human with hold_reading. The outcome run is not gated on crash/not_run alone: marginal cost ~$0, a hold costs no queue time (item 9 is >= 15 h away), and the screen is the only measurement of a 0.5% loss shift; the 50-57% hold rate at x3 is a property of the invented noise model, and T1's noise_j rows are the first real measurement
